reasoning:
**What is asked.** The highest intraday VIX value (the Cboe daily HIGH) from Monday 23 November to Friday 4 December 2026: nine sessions, with Thanksgiving closed and a half day on 27 November.

**What changed since my forecast of 18 November.** Almost everything. I expected the VIX to enter the window near 21.5. It closed at 35.89 on Friday 20 November, up 26% on the day and its highest close since April 2025, after trading as high as 40.03 (Cboe data via CEO Economy, 20 November). The week's closes ran 22.91, 25.46, 24.56, 28.44 and 35.89. The S&P 500 fell 3.7% on Friday to 6,910.39, its seventh straight loss and an 8.6% drop on the week, and the Nasdaq-100 fell 5.6% after Reuters reported that SEC staff are examining Nvidia's accounting (Closing Look and AP, 20 November).

**Starting point.** The peak cannot end below Monday's own high, and the Cboe high includes pre-market prints, which overshoot when futures are weak. After past stressed Fridays with the VIX above 30, Monday's high ran from a few percent to a third above Friday's close, and now and then below it when the weekend brought relief (May 2010). I take a median peak about 13% above Friday's close.

**Inside the window.** Core PCE and GDP on 25 November, thin holiday trading, the OPEC+ meeting on 29 November, ISM surveys and the jobs report on 4 December. The Fed meets on 9 December with a rate hike about 90% priced (Kalshi), so there is no central-bank cushion.

**What would give the other outcomes.** A peak under 34 needs a calm weekend and a rally that holds from Monday's open. A peak above 50 needs another wave of forced selling, as on 5 August 2024 or 7 April 2025. I put that near 20%.

**Forecast.** Median 40.5; middle half 36.7 to 47.0; 5th to 95th percentile 32.8 to 62.5.
